targets.text: colleague adopts the harness mechanics that let Qwen Code drive the same Qwen3.8-27B to finished PRs on this rig — parallel read-only tool batches, an output-token clamp, no per-turn /tokenize round-trip, grep/glob tools, paged reads, tolerant edit matching, spill-to-disk truncation, rule-based microcompaction — and credits Qwen Code (Alibaba) and its Google Gemini CLI lineage in the provenance ledger
Each named mechanism ships as its own small Python module or function with an adapted-from marker, byte-identical to main when its knob is off — no mechanism lands unmeasured

The vLLM adapter sends a bounded max_tokens on every main-loop completion, clamped to the remaining window (port of qwen-code tokenLimits.ts:64-77 clampOutputTokensToWindow: prompt + max_tokens <= window, floor 4,000, ceiling 64,000, escalate-on-length) — today _build_chat_payload (colleague/engines/vllm_openai.py:1023-1027) sends none, so generation is bounded only by max_model_len; the 3h07m / 9-turn / 686,893-reasoning-char run at docs/live-testing.md:99 is the direct consequence

max_tokens = min(ceiling, window - prompt_tokens - margin) is computed from the LAST reported usage.prompt_tokens (or the chars/4 estimate on turn 1), floor 4,000, ceiling 64,000 (COLLEAGUE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), margin max(10,000, 5% of window); a finish_reason=length turn retries ONCE with the ceiling before the existing truncated-turn handling

The per-turn blocking POST /tokenize of the full history is removed from the hot path: window_messages counts the whole message list before every completion (colleague/context.py:270 via the engine counter, vllm_openai.py:830-855) and silently degrades to chars/4 on any error — qwen-code has NO token-count API at all (core/contentGenerator.ts declares only generateContent/generateContentStream/embedContent) and gates compaction on the last response's usage plus a conservative chars/4 estimate (services/tokenEstimation.ts). Exact counts stay available from usage (tokens are never estimated in the artifact)

After the port the loop makes exactly ONE HTTP call per model turn on the happy path (the streamed /chat/completions); /tokenize remains available only for the exact per-turn count in the artifact when COLLEAGUE_EXACT_TOKENS=1, and the artifact still never estimates — usage is the source

Tool calls in one model turn run as ordered batches: consecutive concurrency-safe calls (read_file, list_dir, grep/glob, read-only run_command judged by a fail-closed checker) execute in parallel under a cap, mutating calls stay sequential, results are appended in request order — port of qwen-code coreToolScheduler.ts:1331 partitionByConcurrencySafety + tools.ts:1111 CONCURRENCY_SAFE_KINDS + the QWEN_CODE_MAX_TOOL_CONCURRENCY cap (default 10) at coreToolScheduler.ts:4279; today _run_tool_calls is a plain sequential for-loop (colleague/loop.py:1246-1258)

The batch predicate is fail-closed: only read_file, list_dir, grep_search, glob, view_media, memory recall and a run_command whose argv passes a conservative read-only checker are batch-safe; anything unknown, any edit/write/run_tests/subagent/finish is sequential; results are appended to messages in the model's request order regardless of completion order; hooks/policy/TAE gates fire per call exactly as today

colleague gains first-class grep_search and glob tools (ripgrep when installed, pure-Python fallback; mtime-sorted glob) — colleague/tools.py SCHEMAS has 14 tools and NO search tool, so every code search is a sequential shell=True run_command step; qwen-code selects tools/ripGrep.ts or tools/grep.ts at config.ts:9280-9315 and ships tools/glob.ts

grep_search and glob are repo-confined like read_file (neighbour clones allowed read-only), ripgrep is used when on PATH else a pure-stdlib walker with the same result shape, output goes through the c10 truncation, and both are in CONCURRENCY_SAFE kinds

read_file gains offset/limit paging plus a line cap (1000) and char cap (25,000) that report 'Read lines X-Y of N' so the model can page — port of qwen-code tools/read-file.ts:102 + utils/fileUtils.ts:1447/1475; today read_file has path only and tail-truncates at COLLEAGUE_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=68,000 with no resume (colleague/tools.py:927-939, config.py:88-95); the cat -n grounding (#240) stays

read_file(path, offset?, limit?) keeps cat -n numbering true to the ORIGINAL file line numbers when paged, reports 'Read lines X-Y of N' (and nothing else) when truncated, and defaults stay 1,000 lines / 25,000 chars; a paged or truncated read does not satisfy edit's prior-read check for the unread span

edit_file gains a deterministic tolerant-match tier (smart quotes, line-trim relaxed match that returns the canonical on-disk slice) and prior-read enforcement, with NO LLM repair — port of qwen-code utils/editHelper.ts:313 normalizeEditStrings + tools/priorReadEnforcement.ts (qwen-code deleted Gemini CLI's ensureCorrectEdit LLM corrector: 0 references remain); today edit_file is exact str.count/str.replace only (colleague/tools.py:1017-1042) so whitespace drift costs a full non-ok step

The tolerant tier is deterministic and returns the exact on-disk slice for replacement (never rewrites the model's new_string), tries ONLY smart-quote and per-line trim normalization, and is skipped entirely when the exact match succeeds; a file not read in this work item is refused with a typed error naming the rule

Tool output truncation keeps head+tail (25,000 chars / 1,000 lines; shell 30,000) and spills the full output to a 0600 temp file whose path the model may re-read — port of qwen-code tools/truncation.ts:207 (fs.writeFile mode 0o600, MAX_SESSION_BYTES 500MB at :22) + shell.ts:91; today ToolExecutor._truncate is a tail cut at 68,000 chars with nothing recoverable (colleague/tools.py:838-842)

Truncation keeps head and tail, names the spilled file's absolute path under .colleague/tool-output/ (mode 0600, session cap 500 MB, removed by colleague clean), and the model may read_file it with paging; run_command gets 30,000 chars, other tools 25,000 (COLLEAGUE_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS keeps overriding both)

A rule-based microcompaction floor blanks OLD tool results and inline media (keeping the recent N) before any model-authored fill-line compact — port of qwen-code services/microcompaction/microcompact.ts (831 lines, COMPACTABLE_TOOLS at :40-52, no LLM call) with thresholds modeled on services/chatCompressionService.ts:109-124 (0.85, 20k summary reserve, 13k buffer); today the floor is in-place drop-oldest windowing that inserts one placeholder (colleague/context.py:208-282, loop.py:1270) and invalidates the KV prefix from that point

Microcompaction never calls the model: past the threshold (0.85 of budget, from last usage) it replaces the content of tool results older than the most recent N (default 10) with a one-line marker naming the tool and path, keeps every assistant message and tool_call intact so the OpenAI wire stays valid, records how many were blanked on the artifact, and runs BEFORE the fill-line offer; the model-authored compact and drop-oldest windowing remain as the next floors

The streaming completion gets a three-tier watchdog — request 120s, stream-idle 240s, stream-lifetime 900s, each env-overridable, 0 = disabled — port of qwen-code openaiContentGenerator/constants.ts:1,33,60 (the lifetime cap exists because a drip-feeding gateway resets an idle watchdog forever); today stallguard's floor is 5,400s scaling to 6x mean turn latency (colleague/loop.py:196, 1826-1847) and the #415 silent-turn stall is still open

Three env knobs COLLEAGUE_TIMEOUT (request, 120s today), COLLEAGUE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT (240s), COLLEAGUE_STREAM_MAX_LIFETIME (900s); 0 disables; a trip surfaces as the existing TurnStalled/timeout degradation with which guard tripped on TaskResult.warnings; stallguard's 6x-mean scaling is retired

colleague's base system prompt adopts qwen-code's prompt structure and text where it fits the runtime — Core Mandates, Using Your Tools, Executing actions with care, Final Reminder (core/prompts.ts:278-440, 192-213 lines in the committed snapshots), the headless variant that also REMOVES ask-style tools from the registry (prompts.ts:56-60, config.ts:9348-9356), and per-model tool-call example blocks keyed by model id (prompts.ts:1131-1171: qwen-coder XML / qwen-vl JSON / gemma4 native) — into _DEFAULT_SYSTEM (colleague/loop.py:105-164, 3,970 chars) with an inline adapted-from marker; the env/context prelude stays a first user message (qwen environmentContext.ts:89-100 does the same)

Adopted prompt text is quoted or adapted with an inline adapted-from marker in _DEFAULT_SYSTEM, remains under COLLEAGUE_SYSTEM_MD-style operator override, stays cache-stable (built once), and the headless variant removes tools the prompt says not to call; per-model example blocks are keyed by model id with the current bracket/JSON default when no key matches

Credit lands in three places: a NOTICE file (Apache-2.0 requires notice retention; colleague has LICENSE only, no NOTICE) naming Qwen Code (QwenLM/qwen-code v0.22.2, Apache-2.0, copyright Qwen Team) and its lineage Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2 (Apache-2.0, Google LLC); a docs/adopted-from.md provenance ledger in the docs/skill-sources.md idiom (upstream | origin | what was ported | path:lines | last synced); and an inline marker on every ported algorithm/prompt (adapted-from: qwen-code <path:lines>) — cite-don't-import: algorithms are re-implemented in Python, zero npm/TS dependency

NOTICE names both projects with license, version and copyright holder; docs/adopted-from.md has one row per ported mechanism (mechanism | qwen-code path:lines | colleague path | date); every ported function's docstring carries adapted-from; README + CLAUDE.md link the ledger; no npm package, no TypeScript, no vendored JS lands in the tree

The lineage credit names Google Gemini CLI, not Antigravity: qwen-code README.md:158-160 states 'originally based on Google Gemini CLI v0.8.2 … stopped syncing at v0.1'; its first commit is 'Initial commit of Gemini Code CLI' (add233c50, 2025-04-15); 427 core files still carry 'Copyright 2025 Google LLC'; zero 'antigravity' hits across packages/*/src, docs and git log. The antigravityd in this workspace is agentculture's own daemon, unrelated. Crediting Antigravity would be a fabricated attribution unless the operator has a separate basis
A repo-wide grep for 'antigravity' (case-insensitive) returns zero hits in NOTICE, docs/ and colleague/ after the arc

Every adopted mechanic is runtime-owned and holds under the all-engines rule: batches, search tools, paging, truncation, microcompaction and the watchdog land in colleague/loop.py + tools.py and behave identically on mock (tests/test_e2e_mock.py); max_tokens and stream_options are plain OpenAI-surface keys so the vLLM adapter stays a config-change retarget, and dropping the per-turn /tokenize call REMOVES one of the three documented non-OpenAI carve-outs rather than adding one
tests/test_e2e_mock.py passes unchanged and the mock engine's result shape is identical before/after; the vLLM adapter diff touches only OpenAI-surface keys plus the /tokenize removal

Only the always-on loop guards are adopted — 5 consecutive identical tool calls (loopDetectionService.ts:35) and a 100-calls-per-turn cap (:140), tripping by dropping pending calls (client.ts:3717) — colleague's existing unknown-tool streak guard (loop.py:1240) and step-stall watchdog (loop.py:1872) stay
Five consecutive identical (name + arguments) tool calls or 100 calls in one turn halt the run with a named warning and drop the pending calls — never silently continue

A pre-registered before/after measurement gates each adoption: the same brief (game-benchmark and one real repo task) on both harnesses against this rig, reporting wall-clock-to-deliverable, model turns, prompt+completion tokens, tool calls and success — recorded on docs/live-testing.md the way #421 pre-registers its thinking-effort arm; an adoption that does not move the metric is reverted, not kept

The two arms run on the SAME rig, model and effort table within one day, main vs branch, n>=3 per brief, with artifact ids recorded in docs/live-testing.md; the ratios in c28 are computed from artifact duration_seconds and model_turns, not from prose
Operators running colleague against a local vLLM rig (Ori first), the agents that dispatch through ask-colleague, and mesh peers reading colleague's provenance ledger
The feature doc's first paragraph names the three readers and what each takes from it

A bare colleague work item on this rig finishes real repo tasks in fewer model turns and less wall-clock: every completion carries a window-clamped max_tokens, no /tokenize round-trip precedes a turn, read-only tool calls in one turn run as a parallel batch, the model can grep/glob/page files instead of shelling out, a whitespace-drifted edit lands on the first try, and NOTICE + docs/adopted-from.md credit Qwen Code and Gemini CLI for every ported mechanism
Every clause of the after-state maps to one confirmed requirement (c4–c12, c14, c15) and each has its live-testing row

Today colleague drives the same Qwen3.8-27B as qwen-code on the same rig but with unbounded generation (no max_tokens), a blocking /tokenize POST every turn, strictly sequential tools, no search tool, whole-file reads cut at 68K chars, exact-only edits and unrecoverable truncation — so a task qwen-code finishes as a PR costs colleague more turns and stalls (docs/live-testing.md:99: 9 turns / 3h07m)
The before-state is reproduced on main at the arc's base SHA and recorded in the first live-testing row of the arc

The operator already gets finished PRs from this model through qwen-code; every turn colleague wastes on the same model is a harness defect, not a model limit — and qwen-code's mechanisms are Apache-2.0, measured (its RT doc), and portable as small stdlib Python, so the cost of not adopting them is pure loss
The feature doc cites the qwen-code session usage line and RT doc §1.2 verbatim, with dates

On the pre-registered c22 brief (game-benchmark + one repo task, n>=3 each) against this rig, the ported colleague reaches the deliverable in <= 0.7x the wall-clock and <= 0.8x the model turns of main, with success rate >= main's; the mock e2e suite stays byte-identical; NOTICE + docs/adopted-from.md list every ported path:lines; and a grep for 'antigravity' over the repo returns 0 hits
Ratios are computed from artifacts by script; if either ratio is missed the arc's doc says so and the failing mechanism is reverted or flagged, not kept silently

colleague consumes the lobes 'associate' role as a FIXED, ENUMERATED non-coding seat set — the read-only scout subagent role (colleague/roles.py: provably cannot mutate; #411 cross-role binding, child surface ⊆ parent), the fill-line compact summary author, forced synthesis (#191), the affected-tests/lint digest and rung-2 distillation author rung — resolved BY ROLE NAME from lobes like muse→deepthink; absent = the SAME seats run on cortex with thinking off/low (a resolution rung: the #416 table gains an 'associate' row with a cortex@low fallback), never a per-turn choice; code-authoring seats never route to associate (orin advertises forbidden: code_authoring, repo_action, final_decision, security_decision)

Every associate-eligible seat is listed in one tuple and documented in docs/features/thinking-effort.md's table; the scout child's tool surface is a strict subset of the parent's read-only set; an associate call that returns a repo-mutating tool call is refused and recorded, not executed

The c22 measurement runs THREE arms, not two: main; branch with associate unarmed (the mechanics ratio in c28); branch with associate armed via the spark gateway — so the harness speedup and the associate speedup are attributed separately and neither hides the other
Arm 3 is only claimed once the spark gateway advertises associate (ASSOCIATE_PEER_ORIGIN/PROXY); until then the row reads 'blocked: gateway' rather than being skipped silently

Batch execution splits each call's lifecycle: pre_tool hook, TAE gate and policy gate run on the MAIN thread in request order BEFORE the parallel section; only ToolExecutor.execute runs in the pool; step_index assignment (today len(ctx.result.steps) at call start — would collide in parallel), Step/tool-message append, post_tool hook, progress emit and flight record happen on the main thread in request order after the join — no worker thread touches ctx (challenge pass / concurrency lens: loop.py:1071-1204 _run_tool_call)
Reading _run_tool_call after the port shows exactly one call site inside the pool — executor.execute(name, arguments) — and every ctx mutation outside it

Batch failure semantics are explicit: one call erroring or hitting its own timeout never cancels its siblings (each result is per-call, ok or error, in request order); a flight stop / SIGTERM is honoured at the batch boundary — in-flight tools finish or time out (threads cannot be killed) and the SIGTERM artifact write (loop.py:4958) lands with every completed step; the batch's wall-clock is bounded by the slowest call's own timeout (run_command 300s) (challenge pass / failure-mode lens: loop.py:2274 _flight_stop_requested, loop.py:4958, tools.py:70)
docs/features/work-and-loop.md states the batch-boundary stop latency honestly (up to the slowest in-flight tool's timeout) instead of claiming immediate stop

associate follows the v1.63 opt-in convention, NOT #411 agents mode: COLLEAGUE_ASSOCIATE_MODEL=lobes (or an explicit model id) arms it; a bare run still dials exactly one model and config show lists 'not consumed (opt-in): associate → <model>'; when armed it resolves as a second EngineConfig the way deepthink does (config.py:2301 env keys, :3421 lobes sentinel), and the read-only scout child swaps model/base_url/api_key/effort on its child EngineConfig — subagents.py:594's role.model binding exists only under agents-armed _child_config_for_profile, so it is not the path (challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: config.py:3417-3431, subagents.py:238-270 + :582-604, roles.py)

This refines c33: 'cross-role binding' there means the child EngineConfig swap on a typed read-only role, available with agents OFF; under agents ON the same seat additionally lands on the ledger as a delegation

The c4 clamp window is read live with a fixed precedence — the lobes-advertised context for the resolved role (262144 today) → ONE /tokenize at run start (its reply carries max_model_len, and gives the exact turn-1 count; this is the single remaining /tokenize call) → COLLEAGUE_CONTEXT_BUDGET as the floor — never assumed from the compose default (docker-compose.yml:125 defaults 131072 while .env pins 262144) and never re-fetched per turn; the window source is printed by config show (challenge pass / adjacent-systems + probe: POST /tokenize reply {count:53, max_model_len:262144}; ~/.lobes/.env:57; lobes.py:228)
A wrong window shows up as a vLLM 400 'maximum context length' — the test suite includes that exact server reply and proves the clamp prevents it

The mock engine (the contract reference) gains a batch scenario — one turn returning several read-only calls plus one mutating call — so tests/test_e2e_mock.py pins the batch contract (order, step indices, result shape) on mock exactly as on vllm-openai; today mock.py:97-107 returns one call per turn and would leave batches untested on the reference backend (challenge pass / all-engines lens: colleague/engines/mock.py)
mock and vllm-openai produce the same Step sequence for the same batch — pinned by a shared fixture

grep_search and glob confine paths through the same resolve()-based check as read_file (tools.py:846; symlink escape refused; neighbour clones readable, never written per :852) and the read-only run_command checker is the conservative allow-list form: root-command allow-list, fail-closed on any of ; | & $( backticks > >> < redirections, sh -c, xargs, find -exec/-delete, sed -i, awk system() — qwen-code's own regex checker (utils/shellReadOnlyChecker.ts) is DEPRECATED for a tree-sitter-bash AST parser, which is out of colleague's zero-deps line, so the allow-list stays deliberately narrower; the checker decides ONLY batch parallelism, never permission — the policy gate still gates every command (challenge pass / security lens: tools.py:793-862, :1069-1132; qwen shellReadOnlyChecker.ts:1-45)
docs/features/approval-gate.md gains one paragraph: the batch checker is a parallelism hint, not a sandbox and not an approval

The prior-read set is per work item and is NOT carried across work --continue: a continued run re-reads before its first edit of a file, and the refusal names the rule and the continuation (challenge pass / lifecycle lens: continuation.py:216 rehydrate_snapshot restores a snapshot, not the read set)
The continuation seed body tells the model this rule up front so the first edit does not burn a turn discovering it

With agents armed, every microcompaction blanking appends a ledger event (count + blanked step indices) so ledger_digest and the reconstruction manifest stay truthful about what the model saw; unarmed, the artifact count from h9 is the record (challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: colleague/agents/runtime.py manifest + ledger_digest docstring lines 5-44)
Rehydration from the ledger after a blanking reproduces the blanked history, not the pre-blanking one

Observability: doctor gains informational rows for the stream guards (idle < lifetime sanity), the tool-concurrency cap, ripgrep presence and associate resolution state (consumed / opt-in / fallback); config show prints the max_tokens ceiling and window source; TaskResult carries per-run counts (batches run, calls parallelised, blanked results, spilled outputs, guard trips) (challenge pass / observability lens: doctor.py has no per-seat row pattern today — grep empty)
Every new count is exact (integers from the loop), never estimated

Reversibility: each mechanism has ONE knob whose off-value is byte-identical to main — COLLEAGUE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=0 (no clamp), COLLEAGUE_EXACT_TOKENS=1 (per-turn /tokenize back), COLLEAGUE_TOOL_CONCURRENCY=1, COLLEAGUE_MICROCOMPACT=0, COLLEAGUE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0 + COLLEAGUE_STREAM_MAX_LIFETIME=0, COLLEAGUE_TOOL_SPILL=0, COLLEAGUE_PROMPT_VARIANT=v1 (the pre-arc _DEFAULT_SYSTEM kept verbatim), COLLEAGUE_ASSOCIATE_MODEL unset — listed in one table in the feature doc (challenge pass / reversibility lens: h1 demands it; config.py knob idiom e.g. COLLEAGUE_STREAM=0 at vllm_openai.py:634-645)

The new grep_search/glob tools are the one exception — they are additive schemas; the table says so rather than pretending a knob removes them (COLLEAGUE_TOOLS_LEGACY=1 hides them for the byte-identical proof)

Attribution on copied TEXT (c14 prompt sections) retains the upstream copyright lines, not just a path marker: the adapted-from marker on prompt text reads 'adapted-from: qwen-code core/prompts.ts:<lines> — Copyright 2025 Google LLC, Copyright 2026 Qwen Team, Apache-2.0' (Apache-2.0 §4(c) attribution retention on derivative works); qwen-code itself ships no NOTICE file, so colleague's NOTICE is voluntary credit but the header retention is not (challenge pass / licensing lens: qwen-code LICENSE, ls qwen-code (no NOTICE), packages/core/src/core/prompts.ts header)
Ported ALGORITHMS re-implemented from reading are marked adapted-from with path:lines only; copied prose carries the copyright lines

The c4 output ceiling is per seat, riding the #416 per-seat table shape: acting seats 64,000; deepthink/design seats a higher ceiling (COLLEAGUE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_DESIGN, default 131,072 or the window remainder) so xhigh reasoning is not starved; the same clamp formula applies to every seat (challenge pass / unstated-assumption lens: hard question on c4; effort.py:64-66 seat table; live-testing.md:99 686,893 reasoning chars ≈ 170k tokens on one run)
The feature doc records the 686,893-char run as the reason design seats get a larger ceiling, and the live row shows a design-seat call finishing under it

A proxied lobes role is addressed on the wire BY ROLE NAME: spark's gateway completes {"model":"associate"} through the Orin proxy (probe: 8 completion tokens, reply model nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-NVFP4) but refuses both the raw model id and "worker" with role_infeasible (the same checkpoint maps to the hardware-infeasible local worker backend) — so the associate EngineConfig sends model="associate" and records the SERVED model from the response's model field on the artifact/ledger, never the role name; the associate seat's own effort default is off (Nemotron spends its first tokens thinking: content None at max_tokens 8) (challenge pass / probe: POST /v1/chat/completions via localhost:8001 with model ∈ {associate, worker, <id>})

config show prints both: 'associate → nvidia/…Lightning… (addressed as role name via proxy)'; a gateway that rejects the role name falls back to the model id once, then to cortex@low with a recorded warning
